status: found by reproducing the order in the build session; each is a question for the reviewer — none is resolved by the build

findings.title: A negative supply working capital is admitted, and its negative interest netted against the wheeling interest (West DISCOM: −94.19, −11.77)
findings.detail: West DISCOM's supply working capital is negative — its consumer security deposits (2,767.08) and a month of power purchase (1,470.65) exceed two months' receivables and the inventory — and Table 61 admits interest of −11.77 on it, netted against the wheeling interest of 20.60 to 8.82.  Regulation 38 as the order quotes it makes the interest 'payable on normative basis'; it does not say whether a negative requirement yields a negative allowance or nil.  UPERC's practice on NPCL's FY2026-27 working capital was nil against a surplus (increment 111).  For the reviewer: which reading MPERC's Regulations support.
where: MPERC order on the MP DISCOMs FY2026-27, p.107 Table 61; pp.105–106 (Regs. 23, 38 as quoted)

findings.title: The inventory's GFA base is not printed beside it — it reproduces as the gross GFA at the start of the previous year (Table 55's opening GFA less Table 57's FY2025-26 additions)
findings.detail: Para 2.228: 'one percent of opening Gross Fixed Asset has been pro-rated to two months … divided into wheeling and retail inventory in the ratio of 80:20'.  East's wheeling inventory 21.07 is 1 % × GFA × 2/12 × 80 % only for a GFA near 15,802.50 (West 12.76 → 9,570; Central 20.11 → 15,082.50).  Table 57's opening GFA for FY2026-27 is net of consumer contributions and grants (9,576.28; 5,381.83; 10,900.30), and gives smaller inventories.  The base is presumably the gross GFA; the order does not print it.  The 80:20 split itself holds on every DISCOM.  The inventory enters the binding as a record.  Increment 132: Table 55 prints the opening gross GFA of FY2026-27 for R&M (East 16,845.65); less the FY2025-26 additions of Table 57 (1,043.00) it is 15,802.65, and 1 % of it for two months at 80 % is 21.07 — East, West and Central, wheeling and supply, all six inventories reproduce exactly.  So 'the Gross Fixed Assets for previous year' (Reg. 23) reads as the gross GFA at the start of the previous year.  For the reviewer: confirm that reading.
where: MPERC order on the MP DISCOMs FY2026-27, p.106 para 2.228; p.107 Table 61; p.99 Table 57

findings.title: Table 65's FY2025-26 row 'Equity addition admitted' prints East's and Central's proposed equity (226.34, 197.31); the opening equity of FY2026-27 carries the lower 30 % (181.25, 177.85)
findings.detail: Para 2.241 (c) admits the lower of 30 % of the net addition and the proposed equity, and 2.242 says East and Central claimed the proposed instead of the lower.  For FY2025-26, Table 65's row labelled 'Equity addition admitted during the Year' prints 226.34 (East) and 197.31 (Central) — above 30 % of their net additions (181.25, 177.85) — yet the opening equity of 1 April 2026 is 1,768.44 + 181.25 = 1,949.69 and 2,123.29 + 177.85 = 2,301.14, and Table 59's loan additions (422.91, 414.98) are the net additions less the same lower figures.  The row therefore prints the proposed equity under the 'admitted' label; the computation uses the admitted.  West's (129.20, below its 30 %) is the same either way.  The FY2026-27 rows are consistent.
where: MPERC order on the MP DISCOMs FY2026-27, pp.111–112 Table 65; p.104 Table 59; para 2.241–2.242

findings.title: The wheeling / supply split departs from the Reg. 8.11 matrix as quoted: working capital interest by activity, not 10:90; other income and past true-ups split 10:90 though the matrix does not list them
findings.detail: The matrix the order quotes (pp.120–121) splits interest on working capital 10 % wheeling / 90 % supply.  Tables 75–76 instead put each activity's own computed interest (Table 61) in its business: East 23.79 wheeling and 46.74 supply, where the matrix gives 7.05 and 63.48 of the 70.53; West 20.60 and −11.77 where it gives 0.88 and 7.94.  The order also splits other income and the true-ups of past years (MP Transco's and Genco's passed through, the DISCOMs' own) 10:90, and puts lease charges for smart meters and the R&D fund with interest on project loans at 95:5 — none of which the matrix as quoted lists; deposit interest goes 100 % to supply.  Every figure reproduces with those splits (41 of 48 exact, the rest a paisa).  The effect is on the wheeling charge open access consumers pay.  For the reviewer: whether the Regulations (beyond the extract) provide these splits.
where: MPERC order on the MP DISCOMs FY2026-27, pp.120–122 (Reg. 8.11 as quoted; Tables 75, 76); p.107 Table 61
